chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa from Abd al-'Aziz ibn al-Muhtadi from Sa'd ibn Sa'd said:

I asked him, meaning Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), about a man who had a son whom he claimed, then disowned him, and then removed him from the inheritance, while I am his executor. What should I do? He said: The son remains [in the inheritance] due to his declaration in the court; the executor does not remove him from anything that has been established.

As for what Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari from 'Ali from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Washsha' from Muhammad ibn Yahya from the executor of 'Ali ibn al-Sarri, who said: I said to Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him): 'Ali ibn al-Sarri died and bequeathed to me. He said: May Allah have mercy on him. I said: His son Ja'far married a concubine of his, and he ordered me to remove him from the inheritance. He said to me: Remove him, and if you are truthful, debility will befall him.

So I returned and presented him to Abu Yusuf the Judge. He said to him: May Allah rectify you, I am Ja'far ibn 'Ali ibn al-Sarri, and this is my father's executor. Order him to give me my inheritance. He said to me: What do you say? I said: Yes, this is Ja'far ibn 'Ali ibn al-Sarri, and I am the executor of 'Ali ibn al-Sarri. He said: Then give him his wealth.

I said: I want to speak with you privately. He said: Come closer. So I came close where no one could hear my speech, and I said to him: This one married a concubine of his father, and his father ordered me and bequeathed to me to remove him from the inheritance and not to leave him any share. So I went to Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) in Medina, informed him, and asked him. He ordered me to remove him from the inheritance and not to leave him any share.

He said: Did Abu al-Hasan order you? I said: Yes. So he made me swear three times, then said: Execute what he ordered you, for his word is decisive. The executor said, and debility befell him after that.

Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Washsha' said: I saw him after that, and he did not contradict the first report. Because this ruling is restricted to this specific case and does not extend to others, for it is not permissible to remove a man from the rightful inheritance based on the bequeather's word and command regarding it, nor to rely solely on his word. Rather, he should be left the inheritance share he is entitled to by lineage, and nothing should be deducted from it under any circumstances.
ai.seo_question: Can a father remove his son from inheritance by will, and does the son's status change if he marries a concubine?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Istibsar elucidates the principle of 'iqrar' (acknowledgment) in inheritance law, distinguishing between the specific, limited case of a testator's directive removing an heir and the general rule that lineage-based shares cannot be revoked by mere declaration. The text highlights the scholarly nuance that while the executor's action was validated in the specific instance of Ja'far ibn Ali, it does not create a universal precedent for disinheritance, preserving the integrity of fixed Quranic shares. This reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on the permanence of nasab (lineage) unless explicitly overridden by clear evidence.
